source_text: Huic effecto sine dubio prudentes viri catholici annuerent sacerdotes, videntesque nihil in sensibus carnis, nihil in fetibus sexuum, alterum quempiam praeter Deum verum fecisse; nihil autem Deum fecisse quod malum esset; malumque nihil esse aliud quam voluntatem malam, sine aliquo coactu naturalium delinquentem; pronuntiarent profecto Manichaeos et Traducianos splendentibus catholicae rationis dissiluisse fulminibus.
pass_a_gloss: To this effect without doubt prudent catholic men, priests, would grant, and seeing that nothing in the senses of the flesh, nothing in the offspring of the sexes, anyone other besides the true God made; but that God made nothing that was evil; and that evil is nothing other than an evil will, offending without any coercion of natural things; they would pronounce indeed that the Manichaeans and Traducians had burst apart by the shining thunderbolts of catholic reason.

lemmas.lexica: Julian's polemic label for teachers of tradux peccati
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Sensible men, catholic bishops, would undoubtedly agree to this conclusion. They would see that no one other than the true God had made anything in the flesh’s sensations or the offspring of the sexes; that God had made nothing evil; and that evil is nothing other than an evil will sinning without any compulsion from nature. They would surely pronounce that Manichaeans and advocates of inherited sin had been shattered by the shining thunderbolts of catholic reasoning.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
